results.title: AI Showdown: Gemini vs. ChatGPT vs. Claude - Who wins for what? : Claude by Anthropic Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
results.content: We all lose if you pick just one. They all have their strengths and weaknesses. For example my daughter would prefer to have ChatGPT help explain how to solve a math problem using the Singapore Math Methodology. However, she thinks it is horrible at writing bedtime stories and would prefer to have Claude write her bed time stores as it tends to be more creative and only got better with Opus3. So she uses BoodleBox so she has one place to talk to them all and have them work for her on the things she needs. Another way to look at it, if you hired 3 high powered employees would you keep in in 3 separate offices and only allow them to communicate through you? NO! You would put them in a conference room and unleash their combined power. I constantly have ChatGPT review and draft and then ask [...] You are so right @rohanrecommends. Each AI model has its own strengths and weaknesses, and the best choice for a particular task depends on the specific requirements. For instance, if you're looking for an AI assistant that excels in creative writing and language generation, Gemini and Claude might be suitable options. They're known for their ability to generate coherent and engaging text, making them well-suited for tasks like story writing, poetry composition, or marketing content creation. On the other hand, if your focus is on factual accuracy and comprehensive knowledge, ChatGPT might be a better choice. It has been trained on a massive dataset of text and code, giving it a broad understanding of the world. This makes it well-equipped for tasks like answering factual questions, [...] I constantly have ChatGPT review and draft and then ask Claude to jump in to see if it has anything else to add. We all win when we use them together!

results.title: Equip AI Interview: Ask any question. Natural language response. Instant results | Product Hunt
results.content:
To improve the screening process, we built AI Interviews. If you are evaluating several people (for hiring, but also for a competition say), you can add the same question you'd have asked them on a call and prompt the AI to evaluate like you'd have. For eg, if your question is "What's your favorite pizza topping?", your prompt can be "Award negative points if they mention pineapples".

What's more, you can specify whether the candidate must answer via text, audio or video. Our AI will handle everything at its end. I'll be honest; at least as of now, we are a GPT-wrapper. So, our AI is as intelligent as ChatGPT, Claude, etc. That is, it is more intelligent than you and me :P

Before Viktor, I was bouncing between Manus, Claude, ChatGPT Codex... all of them. And look, those tools are impressive for what they are. But every single one of them still requires me to do the heavy lifting. I'm prompting, copy-pasting, reformatting, uploading, downloading, switching tabs. I'm the glue holding everything together, and that glue is exhausting.  
  
Viktor seems to be pretrained to be an employee. Helpful, asks questions, doesn't leave you on read. He's proactive with asking if he can help with tasks he sees in your email or on your calendar. And he delivers! Quickly.

Jordan Dikoum

#### What's great [...] #### What needs improvement

Since I haven't used it extensively yet, it's difficult to comment on specific improvements. Based on the product information, having clearer visibility into workflow execution, better debugging tools, and transparent usage or credit tracking would make it even easier for new users to adopt.

#### vs Alternatives

I also looked at tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Zapier, and n8n. Those are excellent for AI assistance or workflow automation individually, but Viktor's approach of combining AI with task execution inside collaboration tools like Slack and Teams is what caught my attention.

Josh Crouch
